subject.title: [Bug]: Slack reaction_added/reaction_removed events never delivered via Socket Mode (multi-account, v2026.3.24)

question: Should maintainers keep this issue as the canonical reaction-specific Socket Mode report until live current-main reaction envelope proof identifies the first drop boundary, rather than closing it into broader Slack Socket Mode reports?
rationale: Source inspection proves the handler path exists but does not prove live Slack delivery, and the related broader reports do not carry enough reaction-specific diagnostics to choose a repair safely.

options.title: Keep reaction-specific proof gate
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask for redacted current-main reaction envelopes plus Gateway trace logs before choosing a code fix.

options.title: Fold into broader Socket Mode delivery
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89222 as the canonical report only if maintainers decide the missing diagnostics show the same event-family failure.

options.title: Route under Slack liveness work
options.body: Link this to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77249 only if live evidence shows reactions disappear during a stale or zombie Socket Mode connection.

recommendation.title: Keep reaction-specific proof gate
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask for redacted current-main reaction envelopes plus Gateway trace logs before choosing a code fix.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail points to Slack Socket Mode filtering and current monitor ownership around the affected code path.
